title: Best Badminton Shuttlecocks in India (2026)
summary: Three Yonex shuttlecocks compared: one nylon for practice and two feather for play. Based on shop pages and reviews, not hand-tested.
description: Compare Yonex Mavis 350, Aerosensa 30 and Aerosensa 50 shuttlecocks for India. Nylon vs feather, speed, and who each suits. Not hand-tested.
lead: Which shuttlecock should you buy for badminton in India? This guide looks at three Yonex options: the Mavis 350 nylon for practice, the Aerosensa 30 feather for regular play, and the Aerosensa 50 feather for serious play. We have not hand-tested any of them. We read shop pages, maker claims and a few reviews. We also say clearly what we could not confirm.

picks.name: Yonex Mavis 350 nylon shuttlecock (green cap, slow, pack of 6)
picks.label: For first-timers
picks.verdict: A nylon shuttle that suits practice and relaxed games, though stock may be short.
paragraphs: The Mavis 350 is a nylon shuttle. The maker says its skirt is made to fly like a feather one. Yonex marks speed by cap colour: green is slow, blue is medium and red is fast. The Indian shop we checked (KIBI Sports) lists only the green cap. It says green suits India's usually warm weather, at about 22 to 33 degrees C. The maker's text, repeated by the shop, says it lasts 4 to 5 times longer than ordinary nylon shuttles. That is a seller claim, not independent testing.

Here is what we could not confirm. We could not open the Amazon.in page, so we do not know its rating or return terms. We found no blue or red cap on any Indian shop page. We also saw no Flipkart or Decathlon India listing. KIBI's page showed 11 reviews but no rating or review text. Its stock was backordered with orders paused, so check current availability. The shop's spec field says yellow while its options are cap colours, so confirm what you get before you order.
good: Nylon is usually harder-wearing than feather. Sports Galaxy's guide says roughly 10 to 20 or more games for nylon and 1 to 3 for feathers. Its own replacement table gives a different nylon range.
It needs less careful storage than feathers. The same guide only says to keep it away from extreme heat, like a hot car.
The green slow cap is the one the shop points to for warm Indian conditions.
A reviewer on a US shop page calls it robust for beginner practice. That is a small, overseas sample.
not_good: Sports Galaxy says nylon is not approved for official tournaments. It also says flight and feel differ from feather, and that nylon is harder on racket strings.
Blue and red caps were not found in India. The green cap was backordered when we looked.
KIBI says the skirt hardens in cold air and may break more easily. In heat it softens and the feel changes.
picks.search_query: Yonex Mavis 350 green cap nylon shuttlecock 6 pieces

picks.name: Yonex Aerosensa 30 (AS-30) feather shuttlecock
picks.label: For regular feather play
picks.verdict: A sensible first step into feather shuttles for people who play often and want a natural feel.
paragraphs: The Aerosensa 30 is a full feather shuttle. God of Sports says it has a natural cork base and 16 goose feathers. That shop pitches it at club players who train 2 to 4 times a week. It also pitches it at social players who want a step up from training shuttles. Retailers place it below the AS-40 and AS-50 in Yonex's feather range. God of Sports also says it is BWF approved. That is a seller claim, and we did not check it with BWF.

Some things stay unclear. We found no Amazon.in, Flipkart or Decathlon India listing. Sources disagree on the speed grade. KIBI says medium, while God of Sports says 'Speed 2' and gives no number such as 76, 77 or 78. We found no buyer ratings for India. God of Sports' own editors give it 4.9 out of 5 overall, which is shop opinion, not buyer reviews. Warranty is not confirmed. KIBI's listing was backordered. God of Sports showed Add to Cart without stating stock.
good: Feather flight and feel, which Sports Galaxy describes as the choice for competitive play.
God of Sports' editors score stability and consistency at 5 out of 5. That is shop opinion, not buyer reviews.
Retailers place it lower in the Yonex feather range, so it is a gentler step into feather play.
KIBI lists it as medium speed, which is the usual middle choice.
not_good: Feathers wear out fast. Sports Galaxy estimates about 1 to 3 games per shuttle. That is a general estimate, not specific to this model.
God of Sports says it is not the most efficient choice for high-volume feeding drills. Its editors also score durability lower, at 4.5 out of 5.
Feathers need careful storage in a humid place, because they dry out and break more easily.

picks.name: Yonex Aerosensa 50 (AS-50) feather shuttlecock
picks.label: For serious players
picks.verdict: A higher-grade feather shuttle for experienced players, but not for casual or drill-heavy use.
paragraphs: The Aerosensa 50 is the highest-grade feather shuttle in this guide. God of Sports says it uses special-grade goose feathers and a solid natural cork base. It recommends it mainly for national-circuit players and above, academies and serious clubs. It suggests the AS-40 for city and club players. Pack size depends on the shop. God of Sports lists a tube of 12, while Khelmart lists 2 tubes (24 shuttles). Compare like with like.

God of Sports also makes BWF approval and Olympic use claims, with no source given. We did not check these with BWF, so treat them as seller text. We found no Amazon.in, Flipkart or Decathlon India listing. We could not tell which speed grade Indian listings ship. Warranty and full return terms are not confirmed. Khelmart showed it in stock and God of Sports showed it sold out, so check current availability. One blog reviewer used a single tube of 12. They rated flight 4.5 out of 5 and found it steady, but saw faster wear under smashes. That is one person's view.
good: The shop's own positioning aims it at tournament play.
God of Sports' editors give it 5 out of 5 overall. That is shop opinion, not buyer reviews.
One blog reviewer rated flight 4.5 out of 5. In the reviewer's own speed check, 9 of 12 shuttles landed at about the same distance.
The same reviewer says it still flew well after 200 clears and did not wobble after smash and lift checks.
not_good: It wears faster under hard use. The reviewer saw holes and splinters in the feathers after 100 smashes and 100 lifts.
God of Sports says it is not for beginners and not for high-volume feeding drills.
Feathers need humid storage and careful handling. One shop showed it sold out when we looked.

choose.heading: Nylon or feather
choose.text: Nylon lasts much longer and suits practice, beginners and casual play. Feather gives the natural flight and feel used in competition, but it breaks quickly. Sports Galaxy puts feathers at roughly 1 to 3 games and nylon at roughly 10 to 20 or more.

choose.heading: Check your event rules
choose.text: Sports Galaxy says nylon is not approved for official tournaments. It says BWF-sanctioned events need feathers, while some local events may allow nylon. Ask the organiser before you buy.

choose.heading: Understand the speed number
choose.text: Feather tubes usually carry a number from 76 to 79. A higher number means a heavier, faster shuttle that flies farther. A lower number means a lighter, slower one. For Yonex Mavis nylon, speed is set by cap colour: green is slow, blue is medium and red is fast.

choose.heading: Match speed to your court
choose.text: Sports Galaxy suggests 76 for warm courts (about 25 to 30 C). It suggests 77 for moderate ones (about 20 to 25 C), and calls it the most common in India. It suggests 78 for cool or AC halls. These are shop habits, not an official BWF table, and sources disagree on the exact ranges.

choose.heading: Do a quick speed check
choose.text: Sports Galaxy suggests a full underhand clear from the back line. The shuttle should land between the back doubles service line and the back boundary. If it falls short, try a faster one. If it goes long, try a slower one.

choose.heading: Check pack size, stock and the seller
choose.text: Nylon packs here have 6 shuttles and feather tubes usually have 12. Some shops sell 2 tubes together. Stock changes often, so check current availability. Words like 'BWF approved' or 'Olympic shuttle' are seller text. Buy from authorised sellers and confirm with the maker or event rules.

faq.q: Should a beginner buy nylon or feather shuttlecocks?
faq.a: Most shops and guides suggest nylon for beginners and practice, because it lasts longer. Feather suits players who want the natural flight and feel of competition, but it wears out quickly.

faq.q: Can I use nylon shuttlecocks in tournaments?
faq.a: Not in official ones. Sports Galaxy says BWF-sanctioned events need feathers, though some local recreational events may allow nylon. Check your event's rules.

faq.q: Which speed should I choose for India?
faq.a: Sports Galaxy calls 77 the most common choice in India. It suggests 76 for hot courts and 78 for cool or AC halls. This is a shop guide, not an official table. Try the underhand clear check on your own court.

faq.q: How long does a feather shuttlecock last?
faq.a: Not long. Sports Galaxy estimates about 1 to 3 games each. Hard smashes can wear feathers faster, and dry or AC air makes them break more easily. Shops advise keeping the tube sealed and away from sun and heat.
